_how_to_add: One entry per bot version, hand-kept; the dashboard's Pareto panel (dashboard/app.js, renderPareto) reads this file as it is.
To add a bot: append an entry with id (its name in BOT-NOTES.md), date, kind (plain | search | network | style), parent (an id or null),
what (one or two plain sentences: what it is and what changed from its parent), and the numbers with where each came from:
strength: {a, b, rate, ci, source} -- one BotVsBot result as printed (A's win rate, its 95% interval) between this bot and another bot in this file; null if never played on the test decks.
cost: {total, vs, source} -- BotVsBot's 'N CPU-seconds a game' (the whole game, both bots) against vs (this bot's own id if against itself); null if not recorded.

cost.opp_side (optional): the opponent's side when this was measured, if its cost has changed since (sp-m3 was 1.11 a side before 2026-11-09's skip, 0.87 after); used instead of the opponent's current side.
july: {value, measure: 'order-free' | 'strict', source} -- agreement with people on held-out July 2022; null if not measured.
note: anything else -- an earlier run that conflicts, a number left out and why.
Never write a number that was not measured; no people's names (game ids carry them).
Strength is chained to sp-m3 through the 'strength' links; cost per bot side = game total less the opponent's own side, which comes from its mirror game.

bots.what: The strong bot with sp-m3's trees answering at the root as well (-Dsearch.root): their scores gate the search, name the candidates and anchor the answer, and the only network left is the judge.

strength.source: labels/nn/paired/search-trees-root-vs-sp-m3-test-seed1.out (2026-11-09: test decks, 4 games a matchup, seed 1, 3,168 games, interval by pair; binomial +- 1.7)

bots.note: Matched game for game against the trees alone on the same seed: +5.9 points +- 1.6. It searches 24 decisions a game where the network-rooted bot searched 18.5 (the trees' scores are flatter, so the gate lets more through), which is why it is not cheaper by the whole of the network's 1.1.

bots.what: The trees-root strong bot searching two candidates instead of three (-Dsearch.k=2): two-fifths fewer play-outs and judge readings for the same searches.
